test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 6 Sept 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Three statements are followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they do not conform to real world knowledge, decide which of the given conclusions/possibilities can be true on the basis of the statements.

**Statements:**

1. All cats are dogs.

2. Some dogs are birds.

3. All bears are birds.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some bears are cats.

II. All birds are dogs is a possibility.

III. Some birds are cats.

options.text: Only conclusion I and II are true

solution:
Given Statements:

1. All cats are dogs.

2. Some dogs are birds.

3. All bears are birds.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7542a9d2079f3aa6ec64aaa20ac19ed7544a5239ef5ed821ead27f1b565122c4.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some bears are cats - False (Because, No definite relation given between bears and cats, So, Some bears are cats can be possible only).

II. All birds are dogs is a possibility - True (Because, Some birds are dogs definitely but no information given about the remaining part, so it is possible).

III. Some birds are cats - False (Because, No definite relation given between birds and cats, So, Some birds are cats can be possible only).

So, Only conclusion II is true.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 4".
